settings.heading: Four hours in, the boot gives up.
settings.lede: Every waterproof boot wets out eventually — the outer soaks, the membrane stops breathing, and there is nowhere on a hill to dry anything. This is the layer that is still working when that happens.

settings.heading: The boot is not the last line.
settings.lede: Hill days are long, the ground holds water, and a boot takes it from every direction at once. None of that is a fault in the boot. It is what happens to any waterproof shell worn for eight hours in weather.

settings.title: Wetting out is normal
settings.body: The outer soaks, the membrane stops moving vapour, and what felt waterproof at nine o'clock is heavy and cold by one. Reproofing delays it. It does not prevent it.

settings.title: The ground is wetter than the forecast
settings.body: Bog, tussock, a stream that has come up overnight. Most of what soaks a hill walker arrives below the ankle rather than from the sky.

settings.title: Nothing dries on the hill
settings.body: There is no radiator at the halfway point. Wet at eleven means wet until the car park.

settings.heading: What is doing the work.
settings.head_note: The same sock we sell for everything else — there is no separate, lesser build for one activity. What changes is why each part of it matters here.

settings.title: The membrane is inside the sock
settings.body: A licensed Porelle® waterproof-breathable laminate, sealed between two knitted layers. Water that gets past the boot stops at the sock instead of at your skin.

settings.title: Vapour still has somewhere to go
settings.body: The membrane is breathable in the outward direction, so sweat from a climb moves out rather than collecting against the foot.

settings.title: Crew height, above the collar
settings.body: The cuff sits above the top of a low or mid boot, so the opening in the sock is not level with the opening in the boot.

settings.heading: Worth knowing before a long day.

settings.title: Wear them like a sock, not a liner
settings.body: They go next to the skin with nothing underneath. Adding a liner sock fills the space the boot was fitted for.

settings.title: Adjust the lacing, not the sock
settings.body: Three bonded layers sit slightly thicker than a technical merino sock. If a boot is already snug, the lacing is where you find the room.

settings.title: They wash normally
settings.body: A cool machine wash. No fabric conditioner and no tumble dryer — one coats a membrane and the other degrades it.

settings.heading: Where it stops.
settings.body: Go in deeper than the cuff and water comes over the top, and no waterproof sock behaves otherwise. On a crossing that is above the ankle this buys you nothing — that is a gaiter and a boot problem, not a sock one.
